identity.title: MoE++: Accelerating Mixture-of-Experts Methods with Zero-Computation Experts

problem.claim: Simultaneously improve the effectiveness and efficiency of Mixture-of-Experts methods.

contributions.claim: Proposes MoE++, a general heterogeneous framework combining FFN experts with zero-computation experts.
Introduces zero, copy, and constant experts corresponding to discard, skip, and replace operations, and uses gating residuals to incorporate the previous layer’s pathway when selecting experts.
Distributes negligible-parameter zero-computation experts across GPUs to reduce communication and expert-load-imbalance costs associated with distributed FFN experts.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish MoE++ through heterogeneous integration of FFN and zero-computation experts, including three operation-specific expert types.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report better performance and 1.1–2.1× expert forward throughput versus a same-size vanilla MoE model.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines the goal of improving MoE effectiveness and efficiency simultaneously.
Presents MoE++ as a heterogeneous combination of FFN and zero-computation experts.
Specifies zero, copy, and constant experts, then adds gating residuals so routing can consider the preceding layer’s pathway.
Attributes lower computation, higher performance potential, and easier deployment to adaptive FFN usage and locally deployable zero-computation experts.
Reports improved performance and 1.1–2.1× expert forward throughput over same-size vanilla MoE.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links each zero-computation expert to an explicit operation—discard, skip, or replace—and separately connects those operations to computation and deployment benefits.

lessons.interpretation: Mapping mechanisms to concrete operations and claimed benefits makes the design rationale traceable.
lessons.application: When introducing a modular architecture, name each module’s exact operation and state which claimed cost or capability it addresses.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when module behavior cannot be defined independently or benefits depend on interactions not captured by one-to-one mappings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, model scales, baselines beyond vanilla MoE, statistical details, or which performance metrics support the reported improvement.
The conditions under which the 1.1–2.1× throughput range holds are unspecified.
